answer: Cloned payout keys stall at a one-post watch on a dune berm. A wallet bonds 1.87 POA and sets a 20-byte basalt peg. Over 22 hours it radios five 12-byte hashes, 88 minutes apart, each from a new /28 and folded with the live tip. A grove warden flashes a 16-second checksum tied to the peg and last hash. Auditors void a reused /22, hashes under 70 minutes, or two pegs sharing a 5-byte prefix. Three pegs under one wallet in 14 hours, or two pegs reusing three hash prefixes, pull every peg and hold 1.87 POA for 11 epochs. A late checksum or skipped radio ends the watch; no second peg is issued.
